title: When Plans Change: Lateness, Absence & Delays
summary: Learn how to respond professionally when transportation, illness, family needs, unexpected events, or work delays affect a commitment.
objectives: Recognize when a change should be communicated.
Provide useful status information without unnecessary detail.
Identify responsible next steps after lateness, absence, or delay.

vocab.def: A concise communication describing the current condition of work or availability.
A situation in which expected progress or completion happens later than planned.
Not being present for an expected work period, meeting, or responsibility.
A practical plan for addressing the impact of a missed or delayed commitment.

sections.heading: Plans sometimes change
sections.body: Transportation problems, illness, emergencies, family responsibilities, technical failures, and unexpected work conditions can affect even well-planned commitments.

sections.heading: Communicate as early as reasonably possible
sections.body: Early notice can give supervisors and teammates time to adjust coverage, deadlines, meetings, or dependencies.

sections.heading: Give useful information
sections.body: A professional status update usually explains what commitment is affected, the expected impact, what is known about timing, and what next step is being taken.

sections.heading: Follow the workplace process
sections.body: Different workplaces have different attendance, leave, scheduling, and notification procedures. This course does not replace those policies; workers should follow the applicable process.

practice.prompt: You know at 7:30 that you may miss an 8:30 shift. Should you wait until 8:30 to communicate?
practice.answer: Generally no. Use the required workplace process as early as reasonably possible.

practice.prompt: A project delay affects another team's deadline. What should your update include?
practice.answer: The affected work, current status, likely impact, updated timing if known, and the next step or escalation.

quiz.question: What is the strongest response when a delay will affect other people?
options: Communicate early through the appropriate process and explain the likely impact
Wait and hope the delay disappears
Hide the problem until someone asks
Promise an exact completion time even when you do not know it
quiz.answer: Communicate early through the appropriate process and explain the likely impact

lab.objective: Write short professional status updates for simulated lateness, absence, and project-delay scenarios.
